newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOHO MUTUAL SAYS CAN POST 1996/97 CURRENT PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: TOHO MUTUAL SAYS CAN POST 1996/97 CURRENT PROFIT.

text.p: Toho Mutual Life Insurance Co said on Friday that its ongoing restructuring efforts were having a positive effect and it would be able to post current profits for the fiscal year ended March 31, 1997.
"We can post current profits in 1996/97," a Toho Mutual spokesman told Reuters. Toho posted current losses in 1993/94 and 1994/95, but returned to the black in 1995/96.
Toho said in a statement that it had reduced its foreign securities holdings over the past three years and expected its losses on foreign investment trusts to total only around 2.7 billion yen.

Toho also said it had no property investments carrying large unrealised losses. It said it could post unrealised profits on shareholdings as of March 31, 1997, if the 225-share Nikkei average was above 17,000, an improvement from the 19,000 level required as of end-September 1996. The Nikkei closed on March 31 at just above 18,000.

Toho said its non-performing assets had grown by about three billion yen from 65.7 billion yen at end-September 1996. "We judge that there will be no new emergence of huge non-performing assets," Toho said, adding that it expected to finish cleaning up existing non-performing asset problems "in a few years".

Toho also said it had reduced its average fixed payment rate to policy holders to around 4.3 percent in 1996/97, down 0.6 to 0.7 percentage point from the previous year, thereby helping to reduce the negative spread between investment yields and promised payouts to some 60 billion yen in 1996/97 from about 80 billion yen the previous year.
Toho is slated to announce its earnings results for 1996/97 on June 10, the spokesman said.

Last week Japan suffered its first failure of a life insurance company in the postwar period when medium-sized Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co was ordered to halt all operations except for servicing existing customers. Other insurers have also been rumoured to be in trouble. Friday, 2 May 1997 08:42:40 ENDS nT0274378
